titleStmt.title: Sørge-Cantate ved Christi Grav som i Fasten opføres af Det musicaliske Selskab

work.title: Sørge-Cantate ved Christi Grav som i Fasten opføres af Det musicaliske Selskab

history.p:
Following the previous year's great success performing the 'Passions-Cantata' (SchW B2:306), Scheibe and the young up-coming poet Johannes Ewald decided to produce yet another one which was performed during Lent 1769 at The Musical Society. Similar to the 'Passions-Cantata', the present one reflects new directions regarding Passion music: that is, away from the dramatic type (oratorio passion exemplified by Johann Sebastian Bach) towards a more lyrical with an entirely poetic text (passion oratorio) inspired by Friedrich Gottlieb Klopstock’s poetry. As other passion music by composers such as Carl Heinrich Graun, Carl Philipp Emanuel Bach as well as Scheibe’s and Ewald’s previous cantata, also the present one is in E-flat major. The performance was postponed one day, that is from Wednesday to Maundy Thursday. The new cantata aroused great enthusiasm among the audience, and already on the following day the newspaper, Kiøbenhavns Adresse-Contoirs Efterretninger, published a poem inspired by the performance (the poem is signed by ‘v. W’):
What Evald’s sweet pen and Scheibe’s powerful notes,
At the tomb of Christ have set in rhymes and sorrowful music,
Your society’s Ræhs [i.e. the leader Christian Ræhs] has performed masterfully
Each judicious may be entitled to give you the honour.
The audience in hundreds give you praise and applause;
By diligence plentiful art is your praise and glory.
Only one thing may be said about your entire song of Lent,
That is, that you did not sing it once again.
Continue, precious society! Grow in profusion and honour;
By order, desire and diligence your name shall be everlasting,
Thank you, take the honour for every Tuesday, day of Lent,
Sing often as this year at the victorious grave of Christ.
Though the work received wide acclamation in 1769, it only seems to have been performed once again during Scheibe’s lifetime. No score of the Passion cantata has survived; however, the performance material, which only lacks the solo tenor part, is part of Giedde's Collection. Giedde, who was an able amateur flute player during the late eighteenth century, somehow acquired the instrumental and vocal parts which must either have belonged to The Musical Society, where the work was performed, or have been in Scheibe's possession. Five different scribes including Scheibe produced the part material.

annot.p: 'I Anledning af den af det nye Musicaliske Selskab paa Bryggernes Laugshuus udi Fasten vel opførte Passions-Musiqve. | Hvad Evalds søde Pen og Scheibes stærke Toner | Ved Christi Grav har sat i Riim og Sørge-Noder, | Dit Selskab med sin Ræhs udførte mesterlig | Hver Skiønsom maae med Ret den Ære give dig. | Tilhørers Hundred Tall dig Roes og Biefald giver; | Tiltagen Kunst ved Fliid din Roes og Ære bliver. | Kuns et kan siges paa din gandske Faste-Sang, | Det nemlig, at du ey sang den endnu en Gang. | Bliv ædle Selskab ved! tag til i Flor og Ære, | Ved Orden, Lyst og Fliid dit Navn skal varig være, | Hav Tak, tag Ære for hver Tirsdag Faste-Dag, Syng ofte som i Aar ved Christi Seyers-Grav. | v. W.-*'

incipText.p: Herrens Salvede, som var vor Næses Aand
Han kaldte sig sit Folks forløser
Kommer, Fordømte og skuer det jeg forgiæves tilbød!
Jeg vred mig paa det kummerfulde Leie
Himlens Stærke vaager over Herrens Salvede

physDesc.physMedium:
A set of twenty-two instrumental parts (2 clrno., princ., timp., 2 cor., 2 fl., 2 ob., 3 vl.1, 3 vl.2, 2 va., 3 bs., bc.) nine vocal parts (C.1 (solo), 2 C.1, C.2, T., 4 T. (solo?), B.). Many of the parts have figures at bars and other markings such as question marks in pencil, presumably added during the production of a full score in the 1940s; most of these have, however, been erased, and in that process original pencil markings might also have been deleted (cf. fl.1). Also recent library markings have been added in pencil, usually on front paste down, recto of fol. 1 or on the final folio indicating the total number of pages. Numerous parts are marked with drops and splashes from candles and greases on lower left corner of each folio implying use.
Copyist A: cemb.; canto 1 (a); canto 2; basso
Copyist B: vl.1 (a); vl.2 (a)
Copyist C: vl.1 (b); vl.1 (c); vl.2 (b); vl.2 (c); va. (a); bs. (b); fl.2; ob.1; ob.2; cor.1; canto 1 (solo)
Copyist D: va. (b); canto 1 (b); tenore (b)
Copyist E: bs. (a)
Autograph: bs. (c); fl.1; cor.1, 2; clrno.1; clrno.2; princ.; timp.; tenore (a); tenore (c); tenore (d)
